meta_description: Five phases with named gates — Diagnose, Design, Prove, Industrialize, Compound.

blocks.x: Five phases, each with named gates — engineered to convert strategy into audited production outcomes.
The Method exists to prevent the classic failure mode: strategy decks that never survive contact with production. Each phase ends at a named gate with named signatories — finance, risk, operations.

blocks.caption: Phases and gates
rows: Value Mapping Sprint: portfolio scored on value density, data readiness, regulatory exposure and absorption; baseline metrics locked with owners.
Gate: baseline evidence pack signed by sponsor and finance.
Target architecture and controls: decision/data/agent architecture, control ownership, build-buy-partner decisions, regulatory mapping.
Gate: architecture and control matrix approved by risk.
PoC with falsifiable criteria on client data; adoption probe with the operating team; production-path sketch with run-cost model.
Gate: value memo — go, redirect or stop with documented evidence.
Production build on platform rails: staged rollouts, replay evaluation, SLO instrumentation, evidence generation in-flight.
Gate: outcome SLOs met for two consecutive cycles.
Challenger programs, conformance monitoring, pattern graduation into platform, quarterly value reviews against baseline.
Gate: annual value audit with finance sign-off.

blocks.x: Gates convert enthusiasm into evidence. A program cannot enter Industrialize without a value memo; cannot claim Compound without an annual audit against the original baseline. The gates are the reason roughly one in three PoCs ends with a documented stop — and why the rest scale with confidence.
